title: Accept unit suffixes in parse_duration
statement: Users want to write durations such as '1h30m' instead of counting seconds. Extend parse_duration(text) so that, in addition to the existing plain-integer-seconds form, it accepts one or more components made of a non-negative integer followed by a unit: d (days), h (hours), m (minutes), s (seconds) or ms (milliseconds). Components must appear in descending unit order (for example '2d4h', '1h30m', '45m10s', '1s500ms'), each unit may appear at most once, and whitespace is allowed around the whole string and between components (but not between a number and its unit). The function keeps returning the total number of seconds as a float (so '500ms' is 0.5 and '1h30m' is 5400.0). Reject with ValueError: empty or whitespace-only input, negative numbers, fractional numbers, unknown units, repeated units, components out of descending order, a unit without a number, and any other malformed text. Keep raising TypeError for non-string input. The existing tests in tests/ must keep passing and must not be modified.
acceptance_criteria: parse_duration('90') == 90.0 and surrounding whitespace is still ignored (existing behavior preserved).
Combined components in descending order work: '1h30m' -> 5400.0, '2d4h' -> 187200.0, '1m1s' -> 61.0, '1s500ms' -> 1.5, '1d1h1m1s1ms' -> 90061.001.
Whitespace is accepted around the string and between components: ' 1h 30m ' -> 5400.0; '1 h' raises ValueError.
TypeError for non-string input such as 90 or None.
The return type is float for every accepted input.
